human_tolerance.notes: Breeds in open woodland with taller trees and low cover (English Wikipedia, Distribution and habitat); overwinters in mild urban microclimates such as London, so winter urban use is possible. Classification is a judgement drawn from these sentences.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: French Wikipedia (Reproduction): nesting starts from late April in the southern range and one to one and a half months later further north; a second brood is common in June-July in central and southern areas (English Wikipedia, Breeding). A single start date cannot represent the north-south lag across France.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: DERIVED, LOW CONFIDENCE, NOT A MEASURED WINDOW. English Wikipedia says the species is among the last to leave in late autumn and one of the first to return in spring; French Wikipedia says the same. No licensed French migration-date source was found, and the French wintering minority that the range map shows is not modelled (no winter fraction is sourced).

vocalizations.description: Repetitive 'chiff-chaff' song from a prominent perch, one of the first signs of spring (English and French Wikipedia). Months are a judgement: spring and breeding-season singing, with territorial singing ending after breeding.
Call described as a 'hweet' in English Wikipedia (Description). Used as the alarm-call id by the local behaviour program; no recording is attached.

external.note: iNaturalist taxon 117016 (Phylloscopus collybita, species rank, active) confirmed against the iNaturalist taxa API on 2026-11-01. The iNaturalist identifier is a factual key only.

conservation.note: Speciesbox status LC, IUCN 3.1 (BirdLife International 2024), as quoted by Wikipedia.

range.note: Country list derived from English Wikipedia 'Distribution and habitat' (breeds across Europe and Asia; isolated populations in north-west Africa) and the French Wikipedia range map. Not a gazetteer check; native status for these countries is judged from the breeding-range text.

traits.body_plan.note: Bird: feathers, endotherm and powered flight from the Description and Behaviour sections.

traits.limb_count.note: Two legs; wings are not counted as limbs by the schema convention.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Fly from migration and territory sentences; hop from the Feeding section ('moving restlessly through foliage or briefly hovering'). Hover is not reachable from the local program, so it is not declared.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Endotherm: a bird. The article describes its daily feeding requirement (about a third of body weight in insects per day); the endotherm class itself is standard for birds and not stated in the article.

traits.skin.note: Feathers: plumage, moult and feather description in the Description section.

traits.flight.note: Powered flight: migration and courtship flights described in the English Wikipedia article.

traits.respiration.note: Lungs: standard for birds; not stated in the article.

traits.metamorphosis.note: None: direct development from egg to young bird; standard for birds, not stated in the article.

habitat.resources.note: Invertebrate food from the Feeding section; nest on or near the ground from Breeding; shrub and perch shelter from the breeding-habitat description and the foliage-foraging description. Resource weights are judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Judgement: breeds in brambles, nettles and dense low vegetation (Breeding), so shrub cover is the modelled roost.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg, juvenile and adult stages from the Breeding and Predators sections; no stage durations or scales are sourced, so they are omitted.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The female's nest is built on or near the ground in a concealed site'; domed nest (English Wikipedia, Breeding).

traits.perching.note: Perches in foliage and sings from a prominent vantage point (English Wikipedia, Territory and Feeding).

traits.size_class.note: Derived from mass_kg with the Tiny threshold (< 0.05 kg).

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of the combined sexual range: male 7-8 g and female 6-7 g (English Wikipedia, Description; citing Clement 1995 p.59). Value 7.0 g from the 6-8 g span; not a sex-weighted mean.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: 6-8 g from the male 7-8 g and female 6-7 g ranges.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Proxy from row X=112 of ELEscholer2020_data.csv: S = 0.31 apparent annual adult survival (Clark et al. 2011, mark-recapture, UK, 26 years). Under constant annual survival S, expected age at death counted from hatching is 1/(1-S) = 1/0.69 = 1.45 years. Assumptions: constant survival at every age, which overstates life expectancy where juveniles survive less well than adults; apparent survival, which understates true survival where emigration occurs. The two biases run in opposite directions, so the value is a low-confidence typical-lifespan proxy. Maxima quoted in sources (adults of 3-4 years, a record of seven years) are not used.

traits.diet.note: Authored allocation: the Feeding section states the species is insectivorous, taking insects and other invertebrates. Modelled as 100% invertebrate; no fruit or seed share is sourced.

traits.social.note: Males defend a territory and pairs stay together during the breeding season; birds may join small mixed flocks before migration. Structure Pair with 1-2 birds is a judgement from these statements.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Judgement: singing, foraging and territory activity are described as daytime behaviour; no explicit activity sentence in the source.

traits.defense.note: Judgement. Wikipedia describes males attacking predators near the nest, but the local program models flight to a perch on alarm, so 'Flee' is the main response the program simulates.

habitat.use.note: Judgement from 'moving restlessly through foliage' (Feeding) and 'built on or near the ground' (Breeding).

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Judgement from the breeding habitat description and the note on winter use of urban microclimates.

seasonal.strategy.note: Migration: 'It is a migratory passerine which winters in southern and western Europe' (English Wikipedia lead); French Wikipedia says the species winters in the south and west of Europe. A small fraction overwinters in France (French range map), which the migration strategy does not express; no winter fraction is sourced.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding window in France from the French Wikipedia nesting-start and English Wikipedia second-brood statements. The end of July is a judgement that covers the second brood.

vocalizations.song.note: Song described in both articles. Month set March to August is a judgement from the spring-return statement and territorial singing that ends after breeding.

vocalizations.call.note: Call 'hweet' described in English Wikipedia; no recording attached.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the species-local program bt-chiffchaff-v1 (see species/phylloscopus-collybita/behavior.json).

look.note: Authored from 'greenish-brown above and off-white below' (English Wikipedia lead) and 'yellowish on the flanks' (Description). Colours and proportions are judgement.
